title: Functorial coefficient action on restricted internal Hom
statement: Let C be a small site, R and B sheaves of commutative rings, and phi:R -> B a ring-sheaf morphism. Write r:Mod(B) -> Mod(R) for restriction of scalars [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars], and use the module-sheaf categories [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and internal Hom sheaf [def-pur-sheaf-hom]. There exists a bifunctor H:Mod(B)^op x Mod(R) -> Mod(B), with a natural isomorphism i:r(H(M,N)) -> Hom_R(r(M),N). For every U, b in B(U), h in H(M,N)(U), W -> U, and m in M(W), one has i(b h)_W(m)=i(h)_W(b|_W m). The bifunctor is additive separately in each argument. No flatness, finite generation, or derived-completeness assumption is needed.

proof.text: For each U take the additive group of R-linear presheaf morphisms between the restrictions of r(M) and N to C/U. For b in B(U), multiplication by its restriction defines an R-linear endomorphism of r(M)|U: the scalar actions commute since B is commutative, and the endomorphism is natural by semilinearity of M restrictions. Let b act on local Hom by precomposition with this endomorphism. The identities for zero, one, addition and multiplication, and additivity of the local maps, give the module laws. This includes zero rings and empty sites without exceptions.

The scalar actions commute with restriction to a smaller slice because restricting b along a composite equals two successive restrictions. Hence they define a presheaf of B-modules whose underlying additive presheaf is exactly the usual internal Hom. Its existing sheaf property gives a B-module sheaf. For a section a of R, naturality of phi identifies multiplication by phi(a) on the source with its original R-scalar multiplication. R-linearity of each local map then identifies this action with the ordinary R-action on internal Hom. The identity on local maps is therefore an R-linear isomorphism after restriction.

For a B-linear source map and an R-linear target map, use precomposition and postcomposition on local maps. B-linearity of the source map proves that these induced maps commute with the B-action. Identity and composition hold componentwise; this supplies the bifunctor. The identity comparisons are natural in both arguments. Evaluating their definition gives the claimed precomposition action formula. Addition of target maps distributes under postcomposition, and addition of source maps distributes under precomposition by additivity of the local Hom sections. Thus each partial functor is additive.

mathlib_searches.query: For a homomorphism of sheaves of commutative rings R to B, internal Hom from a B module into an R module has a functorial B action by precomposition with scalar multiplication
mathlib_searches.results: Eight hits: ModuleCat.coextendScalars, ModuleCat.CoextendScalars.obj', scalar actions on ordinary module morphisms, Linear.homModuleOfRingMorphism, homEquivOfIsLocallyBijective, integer scalar action, SheafOfModules.Hom, and DomMulAct actions. No arbitrary-source internal-Hom bifunctor with varying coefficient ring sheaves.

mathlib_searches.query: Internal Hom of a module over a sheaf of B algebras into an R module has a B module structure by precomposition
mathlib_searches.results: Eight hits: ModuleCat.ihom_map_apply, scheme module structures and tilde sheaves, condensed ihom maps, and PresheafOfModules.Sheafify.SMulCandidate. No varying-ring-sheaf coefficient Hom construction.

Seven hits, all ordinary ModuleCat.coextendScalars and its adjunction, not internal Hom over variable ring sheaves. A project-wide node search also found the proved scheme-specific lem-sc-sheaf-coinduction-action, which requires the source to be the pushed-forward ring sheaf; its proof pattern was adapted to arbitrary sites and arbitrary B-modules.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_restrictedCoefficientHomFunctor :
    ∃ F :
      (SheafOfModules.{u} ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat)).obj B))ᵒᵖ ×
        SheafOfModules.{u} ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat)).obj R) ⥤
          SheafOfModules.{u} ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat)).obj B),
      ∃ i : F ⋙ restrictScalars.{u}
          ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat)).map φ) ≅
        ((restrictScalars.{u}
          ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat)).map φ)).op.prod (𝟭 _) ⋙
          Functor.uncurry.obj (homFunctor.{u, u, u, u} R)),
        (∀ (M : SheafOfModules.{u}
            ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat)).obj B))
          (N : SheafOfModules.{u} ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat)).obj R))
          (U : C)
          (b : ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat)).obj B).obj.obj (op U))
          (h : (F.obj (op M, N)).val.obj (op U)) (W : Over U)
          (m : M.val.obj (op W.left)),
          (((i.hom.app (op M, N)).val.app (op U)).hom
            (@SMul.smul _ _ ((F.obj (op M, N)).val.obj (op U)).isModule.toSMul b h)).app (op W) m =
            (((i.hom.app (op M, N)).val.app (op U)).hom h).app (op W)
              (@SMul.smul _ _ (M.val.obj (op W.left)).isModule.toSMul
                (B.obj.map W.hom.op b) m)) ∧
        (∀ M, ((Functor.curry.obj F).obj M).Additive) ∧
        (∀ N, ((Functor.curry.obj F).flip.obj N).Additive)
